extracted.intended_audience: federal agency regulatory analysts (and stakeholders who comment on federal rulemakings)
extracted.subtask_short: regulatory impact analysis for federal rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating regulatory impact analyses for U.S. federal rulemakings, including required analytic elements, categorization and monetization of effects, discounting, and distributional treatment. Also advises how public comments can engage with the A-4 framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the need for the regulatory action
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory impact analysis must include a statement of the need for the regulatory action, covering problem definition, market failure analysis, and legal authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why government action is necessary by defining the problem, identifying any market failures or other rationale for intervention, and citing the legal authority for the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear identification of regulatory alternatives considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis must clearly identify the regulatory alternatives that the agency considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and describe the main alternatives (including the no-action baseline) and explain why each alternative was considered or rejected; ensure alternatives are sufficiently distinct for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of benefits and costs (quantitative and qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis must evaluate the benefits and costs of the proposed action and the main alternatives, using quantitative and qualitative measures as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and monetize effects where possible; when monetization is not feasible, provide careful qualitative discussion and, where possible, non-monetary metrics to inform comparison across alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize benefits and costs into three mutually exclusive categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should categorize benefits and costs into: (1) quantified and monetized, (2) quantified but not monetized, and (3) neither quantified nor monetized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present estimates in each category so reviewers can see what has (and has not) been monetized; maintain mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness across categories to avoid double-counting or omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate benefits and costs relative to a common baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: For each regulatory alternative, agencies should calculate benefits and costs relative to a common baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and justify the baseline scenario (e.g., no-action) and consistently measure incremental benefits and costs of each alternative against that baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified discount rate(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-4 provides discount rate guidance for present-value calculations; 2023 update specifies a 1.7% real discount rate for primary analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the recommended primary discount rate in central estimates and consider sensitivity analyses using alternative rates; document the choice and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributional analysis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses must address distributional effects — how benefits and costs are distributed across affected groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative distributional estimates when possible and discuss impacts on identifiable groups (e.g., low-income households, racial/ethnic groups); include sensitivity and uncertainty around distributional estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of effects on people abroad and future generations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should treat and, where appropriate, include effects on people abroad and on future generations in their analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and, when feasible, quantify transboundary impacts and intergenerational effects; justify inclusion/exclusion and choice of discounting or weighting for future impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater attention to non-quantifiable benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts should give greater attention to non-quantifiable benefits (e.g., equity, dignity, human dignity, nonmarket values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore important non-monetized benefits; document them, explain their importance relative to monetized effects, and where possible provide qualitative or non-monetary metrics to facilitate comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize measurement and reporting of benefits and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular seeks to standardize how benefits and costs of Federal regulatory actions are measured and reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow consistent conventions for categories, baselines, discounting, and presentation so analyses are comparable across rules and agencies; fully document methods, data sources, and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge the problem definition (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective public comments can engage by challenging the agency's problem definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show why the agency's characterization of the problem may be incomplete or incorrect, provide alternative problem framings, and supply evidence supporting the alternative framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide better data on benefits or costs (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that supply improved data on benefits or costs help improve the agency's analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit empirical data, studies, or re-analyses that change the magnitude, distribution, or certainty of benefit and cost estimates; explain methods and provenance of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify alternatives the agency missed (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should identify regulatory alternatives or policy options the agency failed to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe missed alternatives clearly, explain how they differ from considered options, and provide evidence on their likely benefits, costs, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique the discount rate or distributional analysis (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should critique the agency's choice of discount rate and its distributional analysis when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue for alternative discounting assumptions or for different treatment of distributional weights, and provide sensitivity analyses or evidence showing how results change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence on non-quantifiable effects (equity, dignity) (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should provide evidence and argumentation about non-quantifiable effects such as equity and dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document non-monetized harms or benefits, include case studies or qualitative research, and explain how these effects should influence the regulatory decision despite limited monetization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge baseline assumptions (advice to commenters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments can challenge the agency's baseline assumptions used to compute incremental benefits and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unrealistic or unjustified baseline choices, propose alternative baseline scenarios, and show how different baselines change the analysis' conclusions.
